title: PG-001 exact Postgres dependency-only addition during Sprint HOLD

why5.question: Why is a dependency-only governance change required now?
why5.answer: PG-001's existing R1–R4 product candidate requires a PostgreSQL client and its TypeScript types before legal T006 integration, while the canonical Build repo's currently HOLD main lacks both packages.
why5.evidence_ref: GitHub #365 old Draft, exact PG-001 local R4 candidate e2de217; main package.json at 0af8d2f lacks pg/@types/pg

why5.question: Why can these dependencies not be added as an ordinary T006 product change?
why5.answer: package.json is a governance-only path barred during active Task execution and package-lock.json is a HOLD-protected implementation root; directly merging #365 also includes unactivated product code. The separately merged #369 governance repair now provides a narrowly defined dependency-only HOLD transition.

why5.question: What exactly changes, with what preserved?
why5.answer: Add exactly pg@8.23.0 to dependencies and @types/pg@8.23.1 to devDependencies, plus the 15 previously absent npm-registry lockfile package records. The package and lock files are byte-identical to the existing #365 source branch blobs; no existing dependency, existing lock entry, scripts, product code, Sprint/Build state or CLOSED Task is changed.

why5.question: Why is this safer than merging the old PG-001 draft or relaxing normal scope rules?
why5.answer: It preserves HOLD and restricts the entire diff to package.json, package-lock.json and one exact-digest Human approval docket. The #369 validation path denies unrelated files, package upgrades, non-registry lock entries, control-state changes and active Sprint use. Merging #365 as-is would mix products and dependencies while T006 is not yet authorized.
